security_audit.summary: The audit found many static hits caused by Markdown command examples, JavaScript template literals, regex exec calls, and deterministic local media tooling. Real concerns remain around an environment-selected audio engine, storyboard-derived paths that can escape the project directory, and setup behavior that may update global skills from GitHub.

remediation.issue: Storyboard frame paths are not constrained before file reads and writes.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize each frame src, reject absolute paths and parent traversal, and require the final path to stay under compositions/frames before reading or writing.

remediation.issue: HF_MEDIA_ENGINE can redirect audio execution to an arbitrary local JavaScript file.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the override for marketplace builds, or require an allowlisted trusted directory and explicit user confirmation before executing the selected engine.

remediation.issue: Initial setup may update global skills from GitHub without a pinned version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the HyperFrames skill set version and require explicit confirmation before any global skill update or network-driven installer action.

remediation.issue: Several generated HTML attributes use storyboard or audio metadata values.
remediation.suggestion: Escape attribute values before writing index or caption HTML, even when metadata is expected to be locally generated.

content.value_statement: Product teams need launch videos that turn URLs, briefs, or scripts into clear promotional stories. This skill guides capture, storyboarding, brand design, audio, captions, frame animation, validation, and final HyperFrames rendering.
actual_capabilities: Captures product URLs and extracts brand text, colors, fonts, screenshots, and asset descriptions.
Creates a frame-by-frame launch storyboard and narration script for user approval.
Adapts a shipped HyperFrames design preset to captured brand tokens and caption styling.
Generates audio metadata for narration, background music, sound effects, and caption timing.
Builds per-frame HTML compositions, assembles an index, injects transitions, and renders an MP4.
Runs HyperFrames lint, validate, inspect, and snapshot checks before final rendering.
limitations: Requires the HyperFrames CLI and its related local skills to be installed.
Pauses for user approval at brief, storyboard, and final render stages.
Audio and catalog media can depend on HeyGen sign-in or local fallback engines.
Targets product launch and promo videos, not general website tours or topic explainers.

use_cases.title: Launch a SaaS Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a product page or feature brief into a short launch video with script, motion frames, captions, and final MP4.

use_cases.title: Convert a Website Into a Promo
use_cases.description: Capture brand signals and product assets from a URL, then build a promotional story around the strongest proof points.

use_cases.title: Produce a Sales Demo Teaser
use_cases.description: Use a supplied script and product assets to create a polished video that introduces the workflow and call to action.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Basic Launch Video
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request from a product URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a product launch video for this URL: [product URL]. Use a clear value proposition, 30 seconds, landscape format, and English narration.

prompt_templates.title: Use My Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a promo video from this script. Keep the message close to my wording, use the product URL for visuals, and ask before changing the storyboard.

prompt_templates.title: Target a Specific Audience
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a 45 second SaaS launch video for [audience]. Emphasize [pain], [main benefit], [proof], and [CTA]. Use portrait format for social.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Production
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the launch video end to end. Capture the site, propose the storyboard, generate audio and captions, build frames, validate, and render the final MP4 after approval.

output_examples.input: A founder provides a new analytics product URL and asks for a 30 second launch video.
output: A locked brief with audience, angle, length, aspect ratio, and language.
A storyboard with frame summaries, narration cues, asset choices, and transitions.
A rendered MP4 with captions, music, and product-focused motion design.

output_examples.input: A marketing team supplies a launch script and asks to use it verbatim.
output: The script is segmented into video beats without changing the approved wording.
Frames are designed around captured brand assets and voiceover timing.
The final video is validated with HyperFrames checks before rendering.

output_examples.input: A sales team needs a short demo teaser for a new workflow.
output: A demo-led storyboard highlights the workflow, result, trust proof, and CTA.
Audio metadata, captions, sound effects, and transitions are assembled into one previewable composition.

best_practices: Provide a product URL, target audience, desired length, aspect ratio, and CTA before setup.
Approve the storyboard carefully because later visual design and frame work follow it closely.
Use captured product assets and brand tokens instead of inventing screenshots or unsupported claims.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for a neutral website tour with no launch or promotional goal.
Do not ask it to skip storyboard approval when the message, claims, or assets are still uncertain.
Do not add secrets to a project-local .env file for this workflow.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill accept?
faq.answer: It accepts product URLs, marketing URLs, pasted scripts, or briefs for product launch and promotional videos.

faq.question: Does it create the final MP4?
faq.answer: Yes. It renders the MP4 after capture, storyboard approval, frame assembly, validation, inspection, and final user approval.

faq.question: Can it work without a HeyGen sign-in?
faq.answer: Yes, it can continue offline with local engines when available, but HeyGen audio and catalog media may be unavailable.

faq.question: Does it support captions?
faq.answer: Yes. It builds timed captions from audio metadata and applies the selected frame preset caption skin when available.

faq.question: Is it for every video type?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for product launches, product promos, feature reveals, app launches, and commercial URL videos.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
